gaps.sentence: ___ you book soon, there won't be any seats left.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if... not': if you don't book soon, no seats.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ he apologises, I'm not speaking to him again.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' = if he does not apologise; the main clause states the default outcome.

gaps.sentence: ___ the price, the location is absolutely perfect.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from the price' = the only negative in an otherwise positive description.

gaps.sentence: She speaks fluent Mandarin; ___, she reads classical Chinese.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further, even more remarkable achievement.

gaps.sentence: ___ his salary, he earns royalties from three textbooks.
gaps.explanation: 'In addition to + noun' adds one source of income to another.

gaps.sentence: The essay was submitted late and, ___, it ignored the brief entirely.
gaps.explanation: 'What is more' adds a further, stronger point to an already negative picture.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.
